Hi Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track technical alignment before the PoC kickoff.

Call summary (goals you confirmed):
- Validate embeddings + reranker flow for search relevance on your risk models.
- Measure latency and cost at peak (you mentioned ~120 qps expected peak for inference).
- Confirm auth and network posture (customer-managed keys + private peering preferred).
- Prove graceful degradation under quota pressure (429 handling) and deterministic retries for user-visible requests.

Open technical items we captured:
1) SDK & auth: do you want us to ship with Redwood SDK (API key / short-lived JWT) or integrate via OAuth2 client credentials? You mentioned a preference for short-lived tokens backed by your KMS.
2) Request ID / idempotency: we recommend supplying a per-request request-id header (X-Request-ID) for tracing and an idempotency token for non-idempotent ops. Would a UUID per user action be workable on your side?
3) Routing & region: confirm preference to route all PoC traffic to our us-west region vs multi-region fallback.
4) Retry behavior: acceptable retry budget (max retries, backoff) + whether you want retries handled client-side or via Redwood automatic retry policy.

Next steps I propose:
- Attached: a short PoC runbook (finova-poc-runbook.pdf) with milestones and test harness details.
- Please confirm the auth pattern (API keys vs OAuth2 + KMS) and whether infra@finova.com should be included for network/VPC tasks.
- Karthik will put together a request-id + retry recommendation doc and sample header snippet.
- If OK, we schedule a 45-min tech kickoff Wednesday to agree on SLA targets and observability hooks.

Would appreciate a quick reply with the auth choice and whether infra@finova.com should be looped in.

Thanks,
Irene

Hi Irene — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline: 

Auth: we prefer short-lived JWTs issued by our internal auth service (KMS-backed). We can mint on behalf of test identities for the PoC. No OAuth interactive flow required.

Request IDs / idempotency: yes, a UUID per user action works. For background jobs we can include a job_id. Can you share sample code for attaching X-Request-ID and an idempotency token?

Routing: route everything to us-west for the PoC, with a fallback to us-east only if capacity issues arise.

Retry policy: we want client-side retries with a max of 3 retries for user-facing requests. For batched embedding ingestion we expect the Redwood side to do controlled replays (you can keep some windowed caching).

On concurrency: peak expected sustained concurrency is ~120 qps with bursts to ~220 qps for short windows. Typical embedding batch size will be 64.

Looping in infra for VPC peering schedule. Happy to confirm via a quick call — Wed is fine.

—Samir

Hi Samir — thanks for the details, this helps. Short technical plan and concrete defaults for the PoC (we'll adapt after the first 24h of telemetry):

Auth
- Use short-lived JWTs (your KMS); validate signature + kid header on Redwood side.
- We'll support an allowlist for PoC tokens and map them to a test customer id.

Request ID / Tracing
- Please send X-Request-ID on every request (HTTP header). We'll also accept a Redwood-structured tracing header (X-Redwood-Trace) if you prefer.
- For server-generated retries, Redwood will reuse the original X-Request-ID when we can link causal retries to an initial incoming request.

Idempotency
- For operations that mutate state (rare in this PoC), include an Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4). Redwood will store the result for 5 minutes and return the same response for duplicate keys.

Retry strategy (recommended defaults)
- Client-side: exponential backoff with full-jitter. Base=200ms, factor=2, max_delay=5s, max_retries=3 for user-facing requests.
- Server-side (Redwood): for transient 429s, we will attempt an internal adaptive backoff for in-flight batches but only for non-user-visible background tasks; we won't auto-retry user submissions beyond a 1s quick replay to avoid duplicate effects.
- On 5xx we recommend up to 2 client retries with the same backoff.

429 handling specifics
- We return Retry-After where possible. Clients must respect Retry-After; if absent, follow backoff above.
- For quota-sensitive endpoints (embeddings/reranker), we provide a per-request token in the response headers (X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset) to help clients adapt.

Request ID sample (attached snippet):
- Header: X-Request-ID: 8b3d6f8a-3f2a-4c9a-ae9b-7f2f9f0a1b2c
- Idempotency-Key: useraction-<uuid>

Observability
- We'll surface request-level traces in the console and support a link back to your logs using the X-Request-ID.

I'll attach the snippet (requestid-sample-snippet.txt) and a short checklist of what to instrument on your side. If you want, we can include a small middleware for your service that injects X-Request-ID and Idempotency-Key automatically.

Karthik
